To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
1. The PPARgamma gene has been cloned and characterized and its structure is similar to that of other PPARs.

the PPARg2 isoform of the peroxi-some proliferator activated receptor, a nuclear receptor involved in adipocyte differentiation and insulin sensitivity, is a major determinant of insulin resistance and that this effect is mediated through its regulation of the leptin gene.
the PPARg gene expression in human adipose tissue and muscle is increased by insulin resistance, and that the PPARa gene expression is increased in muscle of insulin resistant patients.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the regulation of insulin action and the role of the cytokines of the immune system in the control of glucose homeostasis.
the role of cytokines and hormones in the pathophysiological mechanisms of insulin resistance and the development of diabetes.

the regulation of the insulin resistance syndrome, a condition that affects more than 30% of the population of the United States and is a major risk factor for coronary heart disease, stroke and diabetes.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the adipocyte, as the central metabolic regulator in energy homeostasis, is not only the target but also an active participant in regulating insulin sensitivity and insulin action, as well as the regulation of glucose homeostasis.
insulin resistance is not a disease in itself, but a symptom of an underlying disorder.
insulin resistance is a multifactorial disease, with multiple causes and multiple mechanisms.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have identified a new role for the cytokines of the immune system in the control of insulin resistance.
cytokines and hormones are involved in the regulation of glucose and lipid metabolism in the liver and in peripheral tissue.
the adipocyte is not only the site of storage and release of fatty acids but also a highly active endocrine organ.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the body is not a static thing that is just sitting there waiting to be affected by external factors.

the PPARs have the potential to regulate a broad range of genes that are important in adipocyte differentiation and in adipocyte physiology and that they may have an important role in the pathophysiology of obesity and diabetes.
there’s a lot of room to improve the way we measure insulin sensitivity in humans.
